solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food to set before terrible heathen idol

indicators.note: the word to is placed in front of the rearranged letters that follow
something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters of heathen idol are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dish is being laid out in front of a hideous pagan statue.
explanation.walkthrough: TO comes first, then 'terrible' rearranges HEATHEN IDOL into ADINTHEHOLE. Toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional British dish of sausages cooked in Yorkshire pudding batter, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Photographer's assistants stumble upon police officer with nothing on

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of what follows
in a down clue the zero sits on top of the officer

explanation.surface: Someone trips over a naked policeman, a comic accident.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upon' and 'on' both mean placed above, so each piece sits over the next. DS is a Detective Sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-legged stands steady a camera, so they help a photographer as equipment.

clue.text: He attacks while venerable type crosses city

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'

indicators.note: the saint's letters reach across and so surround the city

parts.note: a saint is a venerated holy person

explanation.surface: Someone is attacked while an old holy figure walks through a city.
explanation.walkthrough: AS then SAINT with LA (Los Angeles) placed across its middle: SAI-LA-NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker or assailant is the person who launches an assault on someone.

clue.text: Having eradicated source of heresy, religious people flower

indicators.note: eradicating removes something, here a letter is taken away
a source is where something starts, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Religious people stamp out heresy and turn to tending a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river (something that flows). HINDUS loses the H that begins heresy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan; a flower in crosswords is something that flows.

clue.text: Ancient Greek chair wrought in bronze

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the colour word

parts.note: bronze and tan are both brownish colours, as of a suntan

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters of chair are reworked

explanation.surface: An old Greek seat has been fashioned from bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronze' reads as the metal, but here it is a suntan colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was a region bordering ancient Greece, and a Thracian came from there.

clue.text: Pass by some houses Palestinians erected

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of these two words are taken

explanation.surface: Some houses have been built by Palestinians.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside housES PALEstinians sits ESPALE; 'erected' turns it upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or slips by, so the verb phrase matches.

clue.text: Extravagant linguistic feature common in Old Norse

indicators.note: the two words are put inside the abbreviations

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for Norse
a verb is a part of speech

explanation.surface: A grammar point is said to be common in the Old Norse language.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Norse gives the abbreviations O and N, and VERB plus LOW go between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblown style is excessive, pretentious and inflated, which is extravagant.

clue.text: It supports conclusions of male nurses in county

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: it is slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Something props up the endings of male nurses working in a county.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of male and nurses give ES, and SEX ('It', as in sex appeal) supports them from below. Essex is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is an English county lying north-east of London.

clue.text: Consumes American energy drink

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone drinks an American energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up something is to exhaust or eat through the whole supply.

clue.text: Member of group at home with drink, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, its sound giving the letters

explanation.surface: A club member is at home with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider belongs to a circle or organisation and has its private knowledge.

clue.text: Fool claiming record is in pristine state?

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the fool holds the record

explanation.surface: A fool insists that a record is in mint condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a stretched definition: pristine here means germ-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the condition of being free from germs, a sterile and so pristine state.

clue.text: Forgets to mention sick son, very neglected

indicators.note: neglected means left out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to be sick is to vomit
S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son is sick and very much ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: VOMIT plus S gives VOMITS, then the V (very) is neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit a thing is to leave it out, so omitting is failing to mention.

clue.text: Chartered accountant hits on Mum's financial security providers

indicators.note: in an across clue the hits come on after the silence

parts.note: mum means silent, as does sh; the 's is the possessive
boxes means hits, as with fists

explanation.surface: An accountant strikes his mother over her financial security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but silence, as in keep mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash boxes are lockable containers that keep money safe.

clue.text: Complicated phase entails delay for collection of waste

indicators.note: to entail here is to contain, so one piece takes the other inside
something complicated is tangled, so the letters of phase are mixed

explanation.surface: A tricky stage of a project brings delay to rubbish collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A slag heap is a mound of mining waste, a pile or accumulation of refuse.

clue.text: Beginning to harmonise thoughts about style for sanctuaries

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
about means surrounding, so thoughts go round style

parts.note: a way can be a manner or style

explanation.surface: Someone starts to harmonise their thinking on style in search of refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: H begins harmonise; IDEAS goes about WAY to give IDEAWAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a secluded retreat, a refuge where one shelters.

clue.text: Paramilitary group originally implicated in Republican Party report

indicators.note: the group and letter go inside the party

parts.note: GOP is the Grand Old Party, the US Republicans
SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter

explanation.surface: A militia is said to be implicated in a scandal involving the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Republicans are known as the Grand Old Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is a rumour or report passed around about other people.

clue.text: A blue star exploded exhibiting chemical property

indicators.note: an exploded star is blown apart, so its letters scatter

explanation.surface: A blue star went supernova, showing a chemical property.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturable describes a substance that can be saturated, a chemical characteristic.

clue.text: Roguish character let down missing international workers

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to fail someone is to let them down

explanation.surface: A rogue disappointed the international workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIL loses I to give FAL, then STAFF. Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, boastful knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is the roguish, roistering knight of Shakespeare's Henry IV plays.

clue.text: Slovenly model lodged in college dormitory on vacation

indicators.note: the model is placed inside the college

parts.note: the Model T was an early Ford car

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A scruffy model stays in a student hall over the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: The model is the Ford Model T; a dormitory on vacation is emptied of everything but its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy means messy and unkempt, as slovenly is.

clue.text: Grave of upper-class male found beneath ancient ruins

indicators.note: in a down clue the gent sits below the ruins

parts.note: Ur is the ruined ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: The tomb of an aristocrat has been found under ancient ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a tomb, but here it is the adjective for serious. The ruins are those of the Mesopotamian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave or serious matter needs urgent, pressing attention.

clue.text: Support mother with questionable sanity

indicators.note: something questionable is doubtful, so the letters of sanity are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone backs up their mother, whose state of mind is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: MA then 'questionable' rearranges SANITY into INSTAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is a chief support, originally a stay rope on a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Americans escalating search for Al-Qaeda's base in state

indicators.note: escalating means climbing, so in a down clue the letters read upward
the letter goes inside the state abbreviation
the base of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Americans are stepping up the hunt for an Al-Qaeda base in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escalating' means the whole is read upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal name for Americans, used especially by outsiders.

clue.text: Message bearer simplified language on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: pidgin is a simplified language for contact between speakers

explanation.surface: A messenger speaks in basic language over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: PIDGIN, said aloud, sounds like the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrier pigeons were used to fly messages home.

clue.text: Sign on relative's food stores

indicators.note: in an across clue the sign comes on after the relative

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, a relative; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A zodiac sign is posted on a relative's larder.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a storehouse for threshed grain, a store of food.

clue.text: Reportedly shift focal point of mass

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say, so the word's sound counts

parts.note: to shift is to change or alter

explanation.surface: It is said someone moved the centre of mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' sounds like physics, but it is the church service; ALTER said aloud gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The altar is the table where the Eucharist is celebrated, the centre of the church service.

clue.text: Expert occupying an area of stage

indicators.note: to occupy is to be inside, so the expert goes into an

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist is taking up part of the theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The apron is the part of a theatre stage in front of the curtain.

clue.text: How sweet fellow starts to understand life is ghastly

parts.note: aw is an exclamation meaning how sweet

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone coos at a man beginning to grasp that life is grim.
explanation.walkthrough: AW, then F, U and L start fellow, understand and life.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and ghastly both mean dreadful or horrible.

clue.text: Lunatic insults clansmen on a regular basis

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter

explanation.surface: A madman keeps insulting members of a clan.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of insults clansmen spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase is slang for a crazy person, a madman.

clue.text: Good-natured, alpha female enters story

indicators.note: the letters come in at the front of the story

parts.note: A is alpha in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A dominant woman walks into the tale and proves friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: A and F come ahead of FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly and easy to talk to.

clue.text: Peace broken by discontented Euopean's envy

indicators.note: the long word is split and the other piece is put into the gap
with its contents removed only the outer letters of the word are left

explanation.surface: Calm is shattered by a disgruntled European's jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: European is printed with a typo (Euopean), which does not change its outer letters; the 's stands for is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is bitter resentment at another's advantages, so resentfulness fits.
